title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Legal Assistant - Conveyancing
description:
Location: Totnes, Devon

Contract Type: Permanent

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience - Circa £24 to £28k

Hours: Monday to Friday

Working Pattern: Office-based

Contract: Full-time

Experienced Legal Assistant sought to join the Residential Property team of a well-regarded and established law firm in South Devon.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Conveyancing Legal Assistant who has a good understanding of the residential conveyancing process from instruction through to post-completion and is looking to join a friendly, supportive and collaborative team.

Position Overview

Working closely with the firm's Residential Property lawyers, you will provide comprehensive support across a busy conveyancing caseload and assist with transactions throughout the conveyancing process.

Responsibilities will include:
- Dealing with new client instructions and initial enquiries
- Preparing estimates and client care documentation
- Assisting with client onboarding, including source of funds requirements
- Preparing and issuing contract packs
- Obtaining property searches
- Liaising regularly with clients by telephone and email
- Supporting matters through exchange of contracts
- Preparing completion statements
- Assisting with completions, including obtaining mortgage funds and sending completion monies
- Handling post-completion administration
- Preparing and submitting SDLT returns
- Dealing with Land Registry applications and registrations
- Maintaining accurate files and progressing matters efficiently
- Working closely with fee earners and the wider Residential Property team

The role would suit someone who enjoys being involved throughout the conveyancing process rather than undertaking purely administrative duties and who is confident working within a busy property department.

Requirements
- Previous experience working as a Legal Assistant within Residential Conveyancing
- Good understanding of the conveyancing process from initial instruction through to completion and post-completion
- Experience with client onboarding and source of funds requirements
- Experience preparing contract packs, searches and completion statements
- Knowledge of SDLT and Land Registry/post-completion procedures
- Excellent client care and interpersonal skills
- Confident communicating with clients by telephone and email
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Ability to prioritise effectively within a busy environment
- Good IT skills and confidence using case management systems
- Friendly, professional and collaborative approach

Benefits
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Enhanced annual leave entitlement
- Additional holiday for long service
- Company pension
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Mental health and wellbeing support
- Free annual flu vaccinations
- Coaching and mentoring
- Modern and comfortable office environment
- Regular social events and team activities
- Firm-wide away days
- Staff discounts on legal services
- Supportive and inclusive working culture
- Long-term career development within an established firm

This is a great opportunity for an experienced Conveyancing Legal Assistant seeking a stable, permanent position within a friendly and highly regarded Residential Property team, based in the heart of Totnes.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Finance Assistant to join the finance team of a large and highly successful business at their Head Office in Plymouth. This role will see you take responsibility for several cost centres - ensuring all expenditure is accurately recorded and reported in a timely manner.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong organisational skills, great attention to detail, and a passion for financial accuracy to join a well-established organisation with a supportive and collaborative working culture.

Key Responsibilities
- Take ownership of a selection of cost centres and balance sheet codes
- Post and evidence monthly accruals, prepayments and other journals as required
- Analyse costs versus budgets and communicate key variances to the Finance Manager team
- Process company expenses and credit card expenditure
- Code expenditure invoices via the data capture system, ensuring payment deadlines are met
- Conduct aged creditor reviews and supplier statement reconciliations
- Support budgeting and reforecasting activities
- Play a key role in meeting month-end and year-end deadlines
- Undertake ad-hoc finance tasks as required

Skills & Requirements
- Financial qualification (AAT or equivalent) preferred
- Previous experience within a similar finance or accounts role

description:
Purchasing & Finance Assistant

Location: Bratton Clovelly

Are you highly organised, detail-oriented and looking to build a career in purchasing and finance? We're seeking a Purchasing & Finance Assistant to join our friendly and supportive team.

Key Responsibilities

Purchasing (60%)

Finance (40%)

- Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.

- Willingness to learn and develop new skills.

Qualifications
- GCSEs (or equivalent) including Maths and English at Grade C/4 or above.
- Further education or relevant qualifications in Business, Finance, Procurement or Supply Chain are advantageous but not essential.

Benefits
- Company pension scheme.
- Generous annual leave entitlement.

- Training and development opportunities.
- Career progression pathways.
- Ongoing support from experienced Purchasing and Finance professionals.

This is an ideal role for someone looking to establish or develop a career within purchasing, procurement, finance or accounts. Previous experience is beneficial but not essential, as full training will be provided for the right candidate.

title: Administrator
description: At Sentinel Healthcare, delivering excellent patient care is at the heart of everything we do. We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team, providing high-quality administrative and reception support across our clinical services. This varied and rewarding role involves supporting patients, clinicians and colleagues to ensure services run smoothly and efficiently. You will often be the first point of contact for patients, so a professional, compassionate and customer-focused approach is essential. The successful candidate will be organised, adaptable and able to manage multiple tasks in a busy environment. Excellent communication, attention to detail and strong IT skills are essential, along with the ability to work accurately and build positive relationships with patients, colleagues and partner organisations. We are looking for a supportive team player who is willing to work flexibly and contribute to a positive working environment. Previous experience in healthcare administration, particularly within primary or secondary care, would be advantageous. By joining Sentinel Healthcare, you will become part of a close-knit team that genuinely cares about making a difference to patients and the communities we serve. If you are looking for a rewarding role where your contribution is valued and every day brings something different, we would love to hear from you. Process electronic inbound referrals from GP's and other healthcare organisations using patient record systems. Booking and managing of patient appointments. Deal with routine patient enquiries. Ensure that electronic tasks are completed in a timely manner. Assist in monitoring generic email accounts. Send text reminder messages/emails to patients. Supporting Senior Administrative colleagues. Attending administrative and clinical meetings as required, which may occasionally be outside of core working hours. General office duties, such as post, scanning etc. Use the e-Referrals system (eRS) and the Electronic Patient Record systems (EMIS & SystmOne) to access inbound referrals and associated clinical documents booked in the Sentinel Healthcare clinical services. Liaise with local Referral Management Centres, GP surgeries and other external organisations as necessary. Using own judgement bring any GP referrals which may be inappropriate to the Clinician(s) attention. Ensure that inbound referrals are appropriately actioned i.e. accepted or rejected. Assist in co-ordinating the utilisation of booking slots across service areas, ensuring that capacity is fully utilised. Any under-utilisation to be reported promptly to the Operations Manager, so that appropriate action can be taken in advance. Re-book and cancel appointments as necessary in the patient record system and ERS. Any cancellations are to be undertaken following the set criteria for the service. Attention should be given to waiting time. Patients must be rebooked within specified time scales. Any problems meeting these criteria, including late cancellations, should be highlighted immediately to the Administration Manager. Ensure that relevant reminders (either by SMS, email or letter, where appropriate) have been sent to patients informing them of appointments. Ensure investigation requests are processed appropriately and results shown to the referring clinician. Assist in completing clinical coding and outcomes. Assist in using the patient record system to ensure that clinical reports and templates are re-produced and sent to GPs (and patients if required) following consultations. Open and prioritise correspondence, ensuring urgent correspondence receives prompt attention. Scan reports and other correspondence into the patient record system in a timely manner. Work closely with service area colleagues/clinicians to ensure good communication and that tasks are appropriately allocated and completed in a timely manner. Adherence to Sentinel Referral to Treatment Rulebook, Referral to Treatment Access Policy and to National Referral to Treat (RTT) waiting times rules and assist in making sure those targets are met. Assist in ensuring that Inter-Provider Transfer Forms (IPT) are completed and sent, as soon as the clinician requests onward referral to Secondary Care, in line with Waiting List Policy (48 working hours). Use other local hospital systems as necessary e.g, EPIC. Ensure that generic service nhs.net email accounts are monitored daily and appropriate action taken in a timely manner. Liaise with GP(s) or their team(s) when removing patients from the waiting lists as per protocols Have a sympathetic and caring manner when dealing with patients, ensuring all queries are handled timely, efficiently and effectively. Deal with telephone queries from both internal and external agencies in a professional manner in accordance with GDPR and statutory policies and procedures. To deal with all enquiries and complaints promptly and sympathetically and inform Senior Management of any problems immediately. Record accurate patient messages and complete information using the patient record system in a timely manner. Request hospital patient case notes (where requested by clinicians) ensuring that relevant clinical documentation (e.g. referral letter, x-rays, other diagnostic results and other supporting information) is available to the clinical teams in the patient record system. Maintain patient case notes and other documentation in good order and arrange return appropriately and in a timely manner. Assist in arranging and attending MDT meetings (where necessary) and ensure that patient notes, investigations and radiology images are available. Work flexibly and collaboratively with colleagues and help to develop a positive, supportive culture. Be prepared to work at various locations to provide appropriate administrative support to clinical teams as required. Attend and contribute positively and creatively to Administration Meetings. Demonstrate a positive, can-do attitude in the workplace. Ensure that resources are used efficiently and help to identify cost savings. Attend and represent Sentinel at external meetings as required Maintain an efficient electronic filing system. Responsible for covering colleagues during periods of annual leave and sickness. Undertake work as directed by the Administration Manager. Adhere to Patient Confidentiality, Information Governance and GDPR policies at all times.
